rationale:
bugs_open/457. rebuild_blog_listing appended an orphan page_components row on every
run and now hard-fails on migration 316's byte-identical guard, which aborts the rerender-pages
workflow before create_rerender_items — so a chrome refresh on boxingonline.com re-renders the three
site_components and then creates NONE of its ~18 child page rerenders.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS ONE LEVEL ABOVE THE INSERT THE BUG FILE BLAMES, and that is what this change fixes.
findBlogListingSlot has four exit paths and only ONE (strategy 1) ever queried page_components. The
other three returned a slot NAME with uuid.Nil, and the caller's test on that nil read it as
"this slot is free". It never meant that — it meant "strategy 1 did not fire". On the motivating page
the plan names no listing-class section, so strategy 2b GUESSED generic-text-block (a slot that page
uses for prose) and the caller appended there, once per run: six rows in two days, all at the
hard-coded position 3, all component_id NULL, each freezing the listing template of its own birthday
into rendered_html. The served page carries 36 cards where 6 belong. Migration 316 did not prevent
the accumulation — all six digests are distinct — it only reported it, on the first run whose render
happened to match a row already present, by failing the whole action.

THE TRAP THIS SUBMISSION MOST WANTS REVIEWED. The obvious fix is to bind component_id (the id is
already in hand — loadContentListingTemplate selects the template and discards the row id). Doing
that ALONE would make things worse: uq_page_components_no_byte_identical_duplicate is
NULLS NOT DISTINCT, so a row carrying a real component_id no longer collides with the NULL-id rows
already there. The loud duplicate-key failure becomes a silent seventh append, and the only
instrument currently reporting this defect is removed. So the occupancy check and the component_id
binding land in ONE commit, occupancy first in the code path — and the write decision is taken in Go,
before the write, never by consulting the constraint.

A REFUSAL MUST NOT RETURN AN ERROR, and this constrains the whole design. rebuild_blog_listing is an
unconditional step of rerender-pages between render_site_components and get_pages, and that workflow
declares no error_step. An error return therefore reproduces the very outage the bug is about. Every
refusal logs at Error and returns a result map with rebuilt:false.

WHY 2b AND 3 REFUSE RATHER THAN CREATE. A guessed name is by construction not a listing slot —
strategy 1 or 2a would have matched if it were. Measured 2026-09-03 16:2xZ across all four live
blog-index pages: ai-agent-orchestration.com and leopardessconsulting.co.uk both already hold a
blog-listing row (1 occupant, so UPDATE), finetuning.uk holds article-grid (strategy 1, UPDATE), and
boxingonline holds 7 rows in the guessed slot (REFUSE). The insert branch is unreachable on every
blog-index page on the estate today, so the conservative rule costs nothing now and removes the need
to defend a judgement about which default is right. Disconfirming result would have been a page with
zero occupants at its resolved slot; there is none.

A SECOND, LATENT DEFECT FOUND WHILE FIXING THIS, included because it is in the same function.
loadContentListingTemplate's function='content-listing' lookup with ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1
is not unique: measured 2026-09-03 there are TWO active rows — the shared content-listing (created
2025-11-28) and content-listing-guides-boxingonline-com (created 2026-09-02). The newest wins, so one
site's fork is currently every site's blog-listing template. They are byte-identical today (same
md5), so this is latent rather than live damage. The fix prefers the canonical row (name = function)
and LOGS the ambiguity rather than refusing — refusing would stop every site's listing rebuilding
while two forks exist, and RFC_034 makes N forks per function the intended future.

NOT DONE, deliberately: no unique index on page_components(page_id, slot_name). LANDMINES records
that it would break 11 legitimate pages where a slot repeats. And the six existing orphan rows are
not touched — paid customer site; the code fix plus one rebuild is the right instrument, and the
per-row identities have been handed to site_delivery_and_editor.

plan.summary: Make every findBlogListingSlot exit path report occupancy, decide the write in Go from (origin, occupants), bind component_id, derive position from the plan, and make refusals non-fatal.

edits.rationale: The caller needs to know HOW a slot name was resolved, because that is what licenses writing there — not the presence of a component id. OccupancyKnown exists so a failed lookup cannot read as an empty slot.
edits.sketch: type blogSlotOrigin int; const (None|ExistingRow|PlanListing|PlanFallback|Default); type blogListingSlot{Name, Origin, Existing uuid.UUID, Occupants int, PlanPos int, OccupancyKnown bool}

edits.rationale: One single-row lookup, run on EVERY exit path — the fix. Uses the shared pageComponentNotRemovedSQL, deliberately WIDER than migration 316's NULL-blind partial predicate, so a row the index cannot see is still counted and the error direction is refusal, never an append. Existing is set only when Occupants==1, never a silently picked first row of several.
edits.sketch: SELECT count(*), COALESCE((array_agg(id ORDER BY position, id))[1]::text,'') FROM page_components WHERE page_id=$1 AND slot_name=$2 AND <notRemoved>

edits.rationale: Returns blogListingSlot instead of (string, uuid.UUID). Strategy 2a now records the plan index so position stops being a literal; 2b and 3 are still resolved so a refusal can NAME the slot it declined. Strategy 1's probe gains the not-removed filter it lacked.
edits.sketch: resolve := func(name, origin, planPos) blogListingSlot { occupancy; on error leave OccupancyKnown false }

edits.rationale: Pure, so the whole table — especially the cases that must NEVER write — is testable with no database. It never consults migration 316; the decision is taken before the write, which is what stops the NULLS NOT DISTINCT trap.

Branch on the decision, not on a nil id. Refusals log at Error and return a result map — an error return would abort rerender-pages before create_rerender_items, which IS the reported outage. The INSERT arm binds component_id and the plan-derived position, and a failed insert also degrades to a result rather than aborting the chain.
edits.sketch: slot := findBlogListingSlot(...); op, refusal := decideBlogListingWrite(slot); if op not update/insert { log.Error; return result map, nil }

edits.rationale: Returns the component id it already had in hand, so a created row is attributable. Prefers the canonical row (name = function) over the newest, because function=content-listing is not unique and ORDER BY created_at DESC was serving one site's fork to every site. uuid.Nil on the built-in default branch — no row, so no honest id, so NULL.
edits.sketch: SELECT html_template, id::text, count(*) OVER () ... ORDER BY (name = function) DESC, created_at ASC LIMIT 1; warn when count>1

edits.rationale: Eight tests, each with a stated killing mutation. Load-bearing: NeverInsertsWhenTheSlotIsOccupied (the NULLS NOT DISTINCT trap, mutation-proven by disabling the Occupants>1 arm), UpdatesTheSingleOccupantWhateverStrategyNamedTheSlot (the root cause), RefusalPathsReturnNoError (the outage), OccupancyErrorDoesNotReadAsAnEmptySlot (the swallow class), and InsertBindsComponentID which reads the INSERT column list rather than a window around the statement — a window scan matches the component_id zap log field three lines below and cleared the one file that was actually violating the rule.
edits.sketch: pure-function table tests over (origin x occupants); two scoped source assertions

edits.rationale: Its anchor for the listing INSERT spelled the COLUMN ORDER and the literal position, so it reddened on exactly the change it should be indifferent to. Replaced with a property-shaped anchor that spans the column list without ordering it; the stamp check still enforces the only property that matters. The sibling save_page_sections entry already records this same lesson about its own over-tight predecessor.
edits.sketch: anchor spans [^)]* across the column list; stamp md5($5)

grounded_in: rebuild_blog_listing_action.go findBlogListingSlot pre-fix: strategy 1 selects id from page_components and returns (candidate, pcID); strategies 2a/2b/3 each return a name with uuid.Nil and issue no page_components query at all.

rebuild_blog_listing_action.go pre-fix INSERT arm: INSERT INTO page_components (page_id, slot_name, position, rendered_html, rendered_html_digest, content_data, build_status) VALUES ($1, $2, 3, $3, md5($3), $4::jsonb, deployed) — no component_id column, position literal 3, unconditional, no existence check.

316_page_components_no_byte_identical_duplicate.sql: unique index on (page_id, slot_name, md5(content_data::text), md5(rendered_html), component_id) NULLS NOT DISTINCT WHERE build_status <> removed. component_id is IN the key, which is the trap; that file's own blast-radius note already credits this action with the check-then-update-else-insert pattern it only half-implements.

[MEASURED 2026-09-03 16:2xZ] duplicate (page_id, slot_name, position) rows with component_id IS NULL, fleet-wide: exactly one group — boxingonline.com /articles/index.html, generic-text-block, position 3, 6 rows, first 2026-08-31 16:29:47, latest 2026-09-02 16:28:02. All six md5(rendered_html) distinct (a49768f2, 2f84ab40, 13ea5fd0, fc99a8b5, 9352d6a2, 5b91bfe5), which is why 316 did not catch the accumulation as it happened.

[MEASURED 2026-09-03 16:2xZ] occupancy of all four live blog-index active pages by (slot_name, position) with the not-removed predicate: aiao /blog.html blog-listing pos2 1 row; leopardess /blog.html blog-listing pos1 1 row; finetuning.uk /blog.html article-grid pos5 1 row; boxingonline /articles/index.html generic-text-block pos2 1 row AND pos3 6 rows. The insert branch is unreachable on all four.

[MEASURED 2026-09-03 16:1xZ] the action's own template query returns TWO rows: content-listing-guides-boxingonline-com (2026-09-02 17:14) and content-listing (2025-11-28 13:36), both md5(html_template)=1b957ae35b08d1236e571b10f59f031d — byte-identical, so latent not live, but ORDER BY created_at DESC selects the per-site fork for every site.

033_rerender_pages_action.sql: rebuild_blog_listing is inserted at {workflow,steps,rebuild_blog_listing} with next_step get_pages, and render_site_components.next_step plus check_refresh_components.else_step both point at it — so its failure aborts the run before create_rerender_items.

Mutation proof run 2026-09-03: replacing the Occupants>1 arm with a disabled condition makes TestBlogListingRefusesToWriteIntoAnOccupiedGuessedSlot and TestBlogListingNeverInsertsWhenTheSlotIsOccupied fail (op becomes insert for plan_listing_slot at 2, 6 and 7 occupants); restoring it returns the package to green.
plan.risks: (1) The refusal is a BEHAVIOUR CHANGE on boxingonline: that page's listing will now never be rebuilt until the six orphan rows are removed, where previously the action attempted a write and failed. Both states leave the listing unrefreshed, but the refusal is silent where the failure was loud, and the discovery check that should file the gap is deliberately NOT in this commit (it needs its own item_type, handler and register entry). Between the two commits the gap is legible only in the action's Error log. (2) Concurrency: the occupancy check is check-then-insert, so two simultaneous rerender-pages runs on one site could both see zero occupants; the second now degrades to a result rather than aborting the chain, but a duplicate row is still possible if their rendered bytes differ. An advisory lock or a 23505 catch would close it and is deliberately not in this change. (3) The canonical-row preference changes which template a site renders with IF the two content-listing rows ever diverge — today they are byte-identical so this commit alters no stored byte, but it does change which row a future divergence would follow. (4) position now comes from the plan index rather than the literal 3; position is not in migration 316's key so this cannot affect duplicate detection either way, but it does change where a newly created listing renders on the page.
